title: Language surface — feature inventory
preamble:
# Language surface — feature inventory

An inventory of every feature the DS language exposes to
rule authors, organised by category.

**This is not the gating catalog.** Most features here are
grammar-level and not dialect-gateable; the BNF parses them
identically regardless of which dialect a rule file
declares. The narrow subset that *is* gateable — action-
level forms that correspond to runtime capabilities a tier
might lack — lives at [LFCA].

This doc earns its place as a **cross-check for the BNF**:
it ensures [LGRA] covers everything
authors can type.

## What this is not

- **Not the gating catalog.** See
  [LFCA] for the narrow set
  of forms dialect registration calls reference.
- Not a grammar. [LGRA] owns the BNF;
  this doc is an informal feature inventory.
- Not a spec for any feature's semantics. Those live in
  per-topic spec docs; this doc points at them.
- Not a source of truth for capabilities. [LCAP.1] is the
  registry, and a program sets them in its `use` block.

### Why most of these aren't gateable

A tier integrator's dialect is an **action-and-capability
allowlist**, not a grammar subset. The BNF does not change
between dialects. Expression grammar, pattern matching,
schema declarations, truth maintenance,
interpolation, and all the grammar primitives are always
available and always parsed identically. Tier authors
cannot invent a different DS; they can only restrict which
actions their tier's rules can invoke and which runtime
capabilities those rules may depend on.
